structs.name: PacketStream_NetPacket_1288_262144_1
structs.size_evidence: no Replay size evidence. Whole .text (0x140001000-0x142400000) scanned for the immediates 265512 (40D28h), 265520 (40D30h) and 263456 (40460h, the PacketBuffer<262144,1312,8> member): no hit (one false positive, 3840D2Eh in Sys_ObfuscatedGuard_FlattenedHashDispatch, and one 734045Fh, a hash constant). No allocation, memset or stride of this size exists. The only 262144-class immediates are 40000h in unrelated code (Path_*, Live_*, bdAntiCheat, ...).
structs.notes: Absent. Every Replay function named for this type is a different object: (1) PacketStream::Create@0x141b60470 (owner, streamIndex 0/1) calls SD_VoiceAllocate and writes fields at +1056/+1057/+1058, a sound voice stream, not a net packet stream; (2) PacketStream::ReadableAt@0x1415e0110 reads this+34604 (0x872C) and calls CL_MainMP_IsPacketStreamReady (@0x1415ed8c0, always returns 1). ReadableAt is slot 12 of the vtable at 0x1424f36e8 (IDA name ClActiveClientMP::vftable, the only code xref to ReadableAt), so it is a client method, not a member of a PacketStream. The name PacketStream_NetPacket_1288_262144_1::ReadableAt exists only as a $unwind$ record at 0x14289f170, which is xdata with no code xref. Replay's packet limit is 1288 (NetLoopback_SendTo@0x1412bcda0 rejects v8+32 > 0x528, i.e. payload 1288), but the buffers it uses are: loopback rings with 32768 data bytes (NetLoopback_InitRing@0x1412bd1c0 memset 0x8000, ring 32832 bytes, 2 channels plus the server ring at loopback+65664), NetThread recv/send rings of 65536 bytes each (NetThread_ctor@0x1412c1330 memset 0x10000 at +44 and +65884), and bdPacketBuffer 10 x 1032 bytes with 1024 capacity (bdPacketBuffer::bufferPacket@0x1421a1730). NetStatic::NetStatic@0x140342f70 does not construct a PacketStream. Residual: a by-value embedding inside a parent whose total size is not an exact immediate, or a loop count form (for example 33189 qwords), was not scanned.

structs.name: NetBuffer_262144_1
structs.size_evidence: no Replay size evidence, same whole-.text scan as above: no immediate 265512, 265520 or 263456 anywhere in code.
structs.notes: Absent. NetBuffer<262144,1> only wraps PacketStream<NetPacket,1288,262144,1> as m_stream at +0 (game-test). No Replay function or string carries the name NetBuffer or PacketStream_NetPacket_1288_262144_1 except the unwind record above; no Replay global, allocation or by-value member has its size. The Replay type that holds the net connection objects is NetConnectionBuffer (s_netConnectionBuffer@0x14D4AC628, NetConnectionBuffer_ctor@0x1410d8fd0, called from NetStatic::NetStatic): count at +0, 602 connection slots of 8 bytes from +8, dirty flag at +4824, thread id at +4828, so at least 4832 bytes. It is not a NetBuffer and holds no 262144 stream. The loopback channel storage is three 32832-byte rings (A118 result, confirmed here by NetLoopback_SendTo's channel offsets 32832 * channel and 65664 for channel 2). Residual: the same caveat as PacketStream (by-value use inside an unscanned parent).
